title: SAT Probability & Two-Way Tables: And, Or, Given, Expected Counts
description:
Probability on the digital SAT is almost never hard math. It's one decision: which total do you divide by? This lesson covers every way the skill is tested, with seven SAT-style practice questions that get harder as you go.

You'll learn:
• Probability as favorable over total, and the complement (not = 1 − p)
• How to read a two-way table and find every possible denominator
• Conditional probability: "given" means restrict to one row or column
• "And" vs "or" (and how not to double count)
• Expected counts: probability × total
• Working backward from a probability to a missing count
• Building your own table from percents (the hardest type)
• A 4-step test-day method

All practice questions are original SAT-style questions written for this video, not official College Board questions. All tables use illustrative data. For official practice, use the free SAT Suite Question Bank (Problem-Solving and Data Analysis → Probability and conditional probability).
